subject: math
title: Unit Rates
seo_title: Grade 6 Unit Rates Worksheets: Rate Language, Unit Price, Better Buys and Constant Speed (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship. For example, “This recipe has a ratio of 3 cups of flour to 4 cups of sugar, so there is 3/4 cup of flour for each cup of sugar.” “We paid $75 for 15 hamburgers, which is a rate of $5 per hamburger.”
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 unit rate worksheets: find unit rates with “per” and “for each”, unit prices, fraction and decimal unit rates, the better buy, constant speed and word problems. 100 practice questions with step-by-step answers and a printable answer key.
key_big: A unit rate is the amount for 1. Divide: 120 miles ÷ 3 hours = 40 miles per hour.
key_sub: “Per” and “for each” mean “for 1”. For a ratio a : b the unit rate is a/b, so 3 cups of flour for 4 cups of sugar is 3/4 cup of flour per cup of sugar. To find the better buy, compare the price for 1 unit, not the total price.
body_html:
The big idea

A rate compares two amounts with different units, like 120 miles in 3 hours. A unit rate tells how much for 1 unit: 40 miles in 1 hour. To find it, divide the first amount by the second.

The words per and for each mean “for 1”. 40 miles per hour = 40 miles for each hour.

Find a unit rate

Example

A car drives 120 miles in 3 hours. What is its speed?

Miles ÷ hours = 120 ÷ 3 = 40. Check: 40 × 3 = 120.

Answer: 40 miles per hour

Unit price

The unit price is the cost of 1 item (or 1 pound, 1 ounce). Divide the total price by the number of items.

Example

We paid $75 for 15 hamburgers. What is the price per hamburger?

$75 ÷ 15 = $5. Check: 15 × $5 = $75.

Answer: $5 per hamburger

Unit rates can be fractions or decimals

For the ratio a : b, the unit rate is a ÷ b = a/b. It does not have to be a whole number.

Example

A recipe has 3 cups of flour for 4 cups of sugar. How much flour is there for each cup of sugar?

Flour ÷ sugar = 3 ÷ 4 = 34.

Answer: 34 cup of flour for each cup of sugar

Every ratio has two unit rates. 3 cups of flour for 4 cups of sugar also means 4 ÷ 3 = 1 13 cups of sugar for each cup of flour. The units tell you which one you have.

RateDivideUnit rate
7 miles in 2 hours7 ÷ 23.5 miles per hour
2 cups of milk for 3 batches2 ÷ 323 cup per batch
9 feet of ribbon for 4 gifts9 ÷ 42 14 feet per gift

Compare unit rates

To find the better buy, compare the price for 1 unit, not the total price.

BoxPricePrice per ounce
12 ounces$3.00$3.00 ÷ 12 = $0.25
20 ounces$4.00$4.00 ÷ 20 = $0.20

The 20-ounce box costs more in total, but less for each ounce, so it is the better buy. To compare speeds, find the distance per hour (or per minute) for each one.

Use a unit rate

Once you know the amount for 1, multiply to find any amount. Divide to find how many units or how long.

Example

6 muffins cost $9.00. How much do 10 muffins cost?

Unit price: $9.00 ÷ 6 = $1.50 per muffin. Then 10 × $1.50 = $15.00.

Answer: $15.00

Example

Zoe walks at 3 miles per hour. How long does it take her to walk 4.5 miles?

Time = distance ÷ speed = 4.5 ÷ 3 = 1.5. Check: 3 × 1.5 = 4.5.

Answer: 1.5 hours

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
120 miles in 3 hours: 3 ÷ 120Miles per hour means miles ÷ hours: 120 ÷ 3 = 40
$4.50 for 3 muffins: $4.50 × 3Price for 1 means divide: $4.50 ÷ 3 = $1.50
Writing “40 hours per mile”Say the units in order: miles ÷ hours gives miles per hour
Choosing the box with the lower total priceCompare the price per ounce (or per pound)
6 muffins $9, so 10 muffins $13 (adding $4)Find the unit price first: 10 × $1.50 = $15

faq.q: What is a unit rate in 6th grade math?
faq.a: A unit rate is a rate for 1 unit, such as 40 miles per hour or $1.50 per muffin. Find it by dividing the first amount by the second: 120 miles ÷ 3 hours = 40 miles per hour.

faq.q: How do you find the unit price to see which is the better buy?
faq.a: Divide each price by its amount to get the price for 1 ounce, pound or item, then pick the lower unit price. A 20-ounce box for $4.00 ($0.20 per ounce) is a better buy than a 12-ounce box for $3.00 ($0.25 per ounce).

faq.q: Can a unit rate be a fraction?
faq.a: Yes. For the ratio a : b the unit rate is a/b, so 3 cups of flour for 4 cups of sugar is 3/4 cup of flour for each cup of sugar.
It is the Common Core Grade 6 standard for understanding a unit rate a/b for a ratio a : b and using rate language such as “per” and “for each”, as in “$75 for 15 hamburgers is $5 per hamburger.”

items.q: A car drives 120 miles in 2 hours at a steady speed. How many miles per hour is that?
c: 160 mile per hour
items.e: “Per hour” means for 1 hour. Divide: 120 miles ÷ 2 hours = 60 miles per hour. Check: 60 × 2 = 120. “60 hours per mile” has the units backwards. 2 ÷ 120 divides the wrong way. 120 × 2 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: A printer prints 150 pages in 5 minutes. How many pages per minute does it print?
c: 130 page per minute
items.e: “Per minute” means for 1 minute. Divide: 150 pages ÷ 5 minutes = 30 pages per minute. Check: 30 × 5 = 150. 5 ÷ 150 divides the wrong way. 150 × 5 multiplies instead of dividing. “30 minutes per page” has the units backwards.

items.q: Jack types 180 words in 4 minutes. How many words per minute does he type?
c: 145 word per minute
items.e: “Per minute” means for 1 minute. Divide: 180 words ÷ 4 minutes = 45 words per minute. Check: 45 × 4 = 180. 180 × 4 multiplies instead of dividing. “45 minutes per word” has the units backwards. 4 ÷ 180 divides the wrong way.

items.q: Owen reads 96 pages in 3 days. How many pages does he read per day?
c: 132 page per day
items.e: “Per day” means for 1 day. Divide: 96 pages ÷ 3 days = 32 pages per day. Check: 32 × 3 = 96. “32 days per page” has the units backwards. 96 × 3 multiplies instead of dividing. 3 ÷ 96 divides the wrong way.

items.q: Sam walks 12 miles in 4 hours. What is his walking speed?
c: 13 mile per hour
items.e: “Per hour” means for 1 hour. Divide: 12 miles ÷ 4 hours = 3 miles per hour. Check: 3 × 4 = 12. 4 ÷ 12 divides the wrong way. “3 hours per mile” has the units backwards. 12 × 4 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: A train travels 260 miles in 4 hours. What is its speed in miles per hour?
c: 165 mile per hour
items.e: “Per hour” means for 1 hour. Divide: 260 miles ÷ 4 hours = 65 miles per hour. Check: 65 × 4 = 260. 260 × 4 multiplies instead of dividing. 4 ÷ 260 divides the wrong way. “65 hours per mile” has the units backwards.

items.q: Luis rides a bike 36 miles in 3 hours. How many miles per hour does he ride?
c: 112 mile per hour
items.e: “Per hour” means for 1 hour. Divide: 36 miles ÷ 3 hours = 12 miles per hour. Check: 12 × 3 = 36. “12 hours per mile” has the units backwards. 3 ÷ 36 divides the wrong way.

items.q: A garden hose fills a 45-gallon tub in 9 minutes. How many gallons per minute flow from the hose?
c: 15 gallon per minute
items.e: “Per minute” means for 1 minute. Divide: 45 gallons ÷ 9 minutes = 5 gallons per minute. Check: 5 × 9 = 45. 9 ÷ 45 divides the wrong way. “5 minutes per gallon” has the units backwards.

items.q: Lily counts that her heart beats 225 times in 3 minutes. What is her heart rate?
c: 175 beat per minute
items.e: “Per minute” means for 1 minute. Divide: 225 beats ÷ 3 minutes = 75 beats per minute. Check: 75 × 3 = 225. “75 minutes per beat” has the units backwards. 225 × 3 multiplies instead of dividing. 3 ÷ 225 divides the wrong way.

items.q: A car uses 4 gallons of gas to drive 112 miles. How many miles per gallon does it get?
c: 128 mile per gallon
items.e: “Per gallon” means for 1 gallon. Divide: 112 miles ÷ 4 gallons = 28 miles per gallon. Check: 28 × 4 = 112. “28 gallons per mile” has the units backwards. 4 ÷ 112 divides the wrong way. 112 × 4 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: A baker uses 24 eggs for 8 cakes. How many eggs does the baker use for each cake?
c: 13 egg for each cake
items.e: “For each cake” means for 1 cake. Divide: 24 eggs ÷ 8 cakes = 3 eggs for each cake. Check: 3 × 8 = 24. “3 cakes for each egg” has the units backwards. 8 ÷ 24 divides the wrong way.

items.q: A school gives out 168 pencils to 24 students. Each student gets the same number. How many pencils is that for each student?
c: 17 pencil for each student
items.e: “For each student” means for 1 student. Divide: 168 pencils ÷ 24 students = 7 pencils for each student. Check: 7 × 24 = 168. 24 ÷ 168 divides the wrong way. “7 students for each pencil” has the units backwards.

items.q: 84 students ride 3 buses to a field trip. Each bus has the same number of students. How many students are there per bus?
items.e: “Per bus” means for 1 bus. Divide: 84 students ÷ 3 buses = 28 students per bus. Check: 28 × 3 = 84. 84 × 3 multiplies instead of dividing. “28 buses per student” has the units backwards.

items.q: Zoe swims 20 laps in 10 minutes. How many laps per minute does she swim?
c: 12 lap per minute
items.e: “Per minute” means for 1 minute. Divide: 20 laps ÷ 10 minutes = 2 laps per minute. Check: 2 × 10 = 20. 10 ÷ 20 divides the wrong way. “2 minutes per lap” has the units backwards. 20 × 10 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: A bean plant grows 14 inches in 7 weeks. How many inches per week does it grow?
c: 12 inch per week
items.e: “Per week” means for 1 week. Divide: 14 inches ÷ 7 weeks = 2 inches per week. Check: 2 × 7 = 14. 14 × 7 multiplies instead of dividing. 7 ÷ 14 divides the wrong way. “2 weeks per inch” has the units backwards.

items.q: A cheetah runs 300 meters in 10 seconds. How many meters per second is that?
c: 130 meter per second
items.e: “Per second” means for 1 second. Divide: 300 meters ÷ 10 seconds = 30 meters per second. Check: 30 × 10 = 300. “30 seconds per meter” has the units backwards. 10 ÷ 300 divides the wrong way. 300 × 10 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: Which rate is a unit rate?
items.e: A unit rate tells how much for 1 unit. “55 miles per hour” means 55 miles in 1 hour. The others compare to 2, 3 or 4 units.

items.q: What does “per” mean in “28 miles per gallon”?
items.e: “Per” means for each (or for 1). The car goes 28 miles for each gallon of gas.

items.q: A car drives 150 miles in 3 hours. Which problem finds the miles per hour?
items.e: Miles per hour = miles ÷ hours. Put the miles first: 150 ÷ 3 = 50 miles per hour. 3 ÷ 150 would give hours per mile.

items.q: Mia runs 9 laps in 3 minutes. She says her rate is 13 lap per minute. What is the correct rate?
items.e: Mia divided the wrong way (3 ÷ 9). Laps per minute = laps ÷ minutes: 9 ÷ 3 = 3 laps per minute. Check: 3 × 3 = 9 laps.

sets.title: Unit price: the cost of one

items.q: 3 muffins cost $4.50. What is the price of 1 muffin?
items.e: For 1 muffin, divide the total by 3: $4.50 ÷ 3 = $1.50 per muffin. Check: 3 × $1.50 = $4.50.

items.q: 4 notebooks cost $7.00. What is the price for each notebook?
items.e: For 1 notebook, divide the total by 4: $7.00 ÷ 4 = $1.75 per notebook. Check: 4 × $1.75 = $7.00.

items.q: 6 apples cost $2.40. How much does 1 apple cost?
items.e: For 1 apple, divide the total by 6: $2.40 ÷ 6 = $0.40 per apple. Check: 6 × $0.40 = $2.40.

items.q: 3 pounds of chicken cost $9.60. What is the price per pound?
items.e: For 1 pound, divide the total by 3: $9.60 ÷ 3 = $3.20 per pound. Check: 3 × $3.20 = $9.60.

items.q: We paid $75 for 15 hamburgers. What is the rate per hamburger?
items.e: For 1 hamburger, divide the total by 15: $75.00 ÷ 15 = $5.00 per hamburger. Check: 15 × $5.00 = $75.00. So $75 for 15 hamburgers is a rate of $5 per hamburger.

items.q: A 12-ounce box of cereal costs $3.84. What is the price per ounce?
items.e: For 1 ounce, divide the total by 12: $3.84 ÷ 12 = $0.32 per ounce. Check: 12 × $0.32 = $3.84. A store shelf tag often shows this unit price.

items.q: A pack of 8 pencils costs $2.00. What does 1 pencil cost?
items.e: For 1 pencil, divide the total by 8: $2.00 ÷ 8 = $0.25 per pencil. Check: 8 × $0.25 = $2.00.

items.q: A 5-pound bag of apples costs $6.45. What is the price per pound?
items.e: For 1 pound, divide the total by 5: $6.45 ÷ 5 = $1.29 per pound. Check: 5 × $1.29 = $6.45.

items.q: 5 bus tickets cost $12.50. What is the price of 1 ticket?
items.e: For 1 ticket, divide the total by 5: $12.50 ÷ 5 = $2.50 per ticket. Check: 5 × $2.50 = $12.50.

items.q: Maya pays $38.40 for 12 gallons of gas. What is the price per gallon?
items.e: For 1 gallon, divide the total by 12: $38.40 ÷ 12 = $3.20 per gallon. Check: 12 × $3.20 = $38.40.

items.q: Sofia earns $72 for 6 hours of babysitting. How much does she earn per hour?
items.e: For 1 hour, divide the total by 6: $72.00 ÷ 6 = $12.00 per hour. Check: 6 × $12.00 = $72.00.

items.q: A 6-pack of water costs $4.20. How much is that per bottle?
items.e: For 1 bottle, divide the total by 6: $4.20 ÷ 6 = $0.70 per bottle. Check: 6 × $0.70 = $4.20.

items.q: A bunch of 6 bananas costs $1.50. What does each banana cost?
items.e: For 1 banana, divide the total by 6: $1.50 ÷ 6 = $0.25 per banana. Check: 6 × $0.25 = $1.50.

items.q: A 2-pound bag of grapes costs $5.98. What is the price per pound?
items.e: For 1 pound, divide the total by 2: $5.98 ÷ 2 = $2.99 per pound. Check: 2 × $2.99 = $5.98.

items.q: A case of 24 cans of juice costs $10.80. What is the price per can?
items.e: For 1 can, divide the total by 24: $10.80 ÷ 24 = $0.45 per can. Check: 24 × $0.45 = $10.80.

items.q: 4 movie tickets cost $54. What is the price of 1 ticket?
items.e: For 1 ticket, divide the total by 4: $54.00 ÷ 4 = $13.50 per ticket. Check: 4 × $13.50 = $54.00.

items.q: A 16-ounce block of cheese costs $4.00. What is the price per ounce?
items.e: For 1 ounce, divide the total by 16: $4.00 ÷ 16 = $0.25 per ounce. Check: 16 × $0.25 = $4.00.

items.q: Parking costs $9.00 for 3 hours. What is the cost per hour?
items.e: For 1 hour, divide the total by 3: $9.00 ÷ 3 = $3.00 per hour. Check: 3 × $3.00 = $9.00.

items.q: 4 pens cost $3.00. Which problem finds the price of 1 pen?
items.e: The price for 1 pen is the total price shared into 4 equal parts: $3.00 ÷ 4 = $0.75. 4 ÷ 3.00 divides the wrong way: it tells how many pens you get for $1.

items.q: A 5-pound bag of rice costs $4.00. Ava says rice costs $1.25 per pound. What is the correct price per pound?
items.e: Ava divided 5 ÷ 4, the wrong way. Price per pound = dollars ÷ pounds: $4.00 ÷ 5 = $0.80. Check: 5 × $0.80 = $4.00. ($1.25 is how many pounds you get for $1.)

sets.title: Unit rates with fractions and decimals

items.q: A recipe uses 3 cups of flour for 4 cups of sugar. How many cups of flour are there for each cup of sugar?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 cup of sugar, divide: 3 ÷ 4 = 34 cup. Check: 34 × 4 = 3. (4 ÷ 3 divides the wrong way.) So the ratio 3 : 4 has the unit rate 34 cup of flour per cup of sugar.

items.q: Nora uses 2 cups of milk for 3 batches of pancakes. How much milk is that per batch?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 batch, divide: 2 ÷ 3 = 23 cup. Check: 23 × 3 = 2. (3 ÷ 2 divides the wrong way.)

items.q: 8 friends share 5 pizzas equally. How much pizza does each friend get?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 friend, divide: 5 ÷ 8 = 58 pizza. Check: 58 × 8 = 5. (8 ÷ 5 divides the wrong way.)

items.q: Ben feeds his dog 5 pounds of food in 2 days. How much food is that per day?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 day, divide: 5 ÷ 2 = 2 12 pounds. Check: 2 12 × 2 = 5. (2 ÷ 5 divides the wrong way.)

items.q: Omar walks 7 miles in 2 hours. What is his speed in miles per hour?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 hour, divide: 7 ÷ 2 = 3.5 miles per hour. Check: 3.5 × 2 = 7. (2 ÷ 7 divides the wrong way.)

items.q: A painter uses 2 gallons of paint for 5 walls of the same size. How much paint is that for each wall?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 wall, divide: 2 ÷ 5 = 25 gallon. Check: 25 × 5 = 2. (5 ÷ 2 divides the wrong way.)

items.q: Noah uses 9 feet of ribbon to wrap 4 gifts. How much ribbon is that per gift?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 gift, divide: 9 ÷ 4 = 2 14 feet. Check: 2 14 × 4 = 9. (4 ÷ 9 divides the wrong way.)

items.q: A tap fills a 15-liter bucket in 6 minutes. How many liters per minute does it fill?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 minute, divide: 15 ÷ 6 = 2.5 liters. Check: 2.5 × 6 = 15. (6 ÷ 15 divides the wrong way.)

items.q: 3 inches of rain fell in 12 hours. How much rain fell per hour?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 hour, divide: 3 ÷ 12 = 312 = 14 inch. Check: 14 × 12 = 3. (12 ÷ 3 divides the wrong way.)

items.q: A bean plant grows 9 centimeters in 6 days. How many centimeters per day does it grow?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 day, divide: 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5 centimeters. Check: 1.5 × 6 = 9. (6 ÷ 9 divides the wrong way.)

items.q: A car goes 150 miles on 4 gallons of gas. How many miles per gallon does it get?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 gallon, divide: 150 ÷ 4 = 37.5 miles. Check: 37.5 × 4 = 150. (4 ÷ 150 divides the wrong way.)

items.q: A recipe uses 3 cups of flour for 4 cups of sugar. How many cups of sugar are there for each cup of flour?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 cup of flour, divide: 4 ÷ 3 = 1 13 cups. Check: 1 13 × 3 = 4. (3 ÷ 4 divides the wrong way.) Every ratio has two unit rates: 34 cup of flour per cup of sugar, and 1 13 cups of sugar per cup of flour.

items.q: Ruby swims 6 laps in 8 minutes. How many laps per minute does she swim?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 minute, divide: 6 ÷ 8 = 68 = 34 lap. Check: 34 × 8 = 6. (8 ÷ 6 divides the wrong way.)

items.q: A lemonade recipe uses 6 lemons for 4 cups of lemonade. How many lemons are used for each cup?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 cup, divide: 6 ÷ 4 = 64 = 1 12 lemons. Check: 1 12 × 4 = 6. (4 ÷ 6 divides the wrong way.)

items.q: Grace rides a bike 27 miles in 2 hours. What is her speed in miles per hour?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 hour, divide: 27 ÷ 2 = 13.5 miles per hour. Check: 13.5 × 2 = 27. (2 ÷ 27 divides the wrong way.)

items.q: 5 inches of snow fell in 4 hours. How many inches fell per hour?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 hour, divide: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 14 inches. Check: 1 14 × 4 = 5. (4 ÷ 5 divides the wrong way.)

items.q: 3 yards of fabric make 8 pillows. How much fabric is used for each pillow?
items.e: To find the amount for 1 pillow, divide: 3 ÷ 8 = 38 yard. Check: 38 × 8 = 3. (8 ÷ 3 divides the wrong way.)

items.q: Kai runs 5 kilometers in 25 minutes. How many minutes does he take per kilometer?
items.e: Now the minutes come first: minutes ÷ kilometers = 25 ÷ 5 = 5 minutes per kilometer. (The other unit rate is 5 ÷ 25 = 15 kilometer per minute.)

items.q: What is the unit rate a/b for the ratio 2 : 5?
items.e: For the ratio a : b, the unit rate is a ÷ b. 2 ÷ 5 = 25. It means 25 of the first amount for each 1 of the second amount.

items.q: A club has 4 teachers for 60 students. Which sentence uses rate language correctly?
c: There are 15 students for each teacher.
There are 15 teachers for each student.
There are 60 students for each teacher.
There are 4 students for each teacher.
items.e: Students per teacher = 60 ÷ 4 = 15, so there are 15 students for each teacher. “15 teachers for each student” swaps the units.

sets.title: Compare unit rates: the better buy and the faster speed

items.q:
Which is the better buy?
Box A: 12 ounces of cereal for $3.00
Box B: 20 ounces of cereal for $4.00
c: Both cost the same per ounce
items.e: Compare the price for 1 ounce, not the total price. Box A: $3.00 ÷ 12 = $0.25 per ounce. Box B: $4.00 ÷ 20 = $0.20 per ounce. Box B costs less per ounce, so it is the better buy. (Box A costs less in total, but you get less.)

items.q:
Which is the better buy?
Bottle A: 64 ounces of juice for $3.84
Bottle B: 32 ounces of juice for $2.24
c: Both cost the same per ounce
items.e: Compare the price for 1 ounce, not the total price. Bottle A: $3.84 ÷ 64 = $0.06 per ounce. Bottle B: $2.24 ÷ 32 = $0.07 per ounce. Bottle A costs less per ounce, so it is the better buy. (Bottle B costs less in total, but you get less.)

items.q:
Which is the better buy?
Bag A: 1 pound of pasta for $1.50
Bag B: 3 pounds of pasta for $4.20
c: Both cost the same per pound
items.e: Compare the price for 1 pound, not the total price. Bag A: $1.50 ÷ 1 = $1.50 per pound. Bag B: $4.20 ÷ 3 = $1.40 per pound. Bag B costs less per pound, so it is the better buy. (Bag A costs less in total, but you get less.)

items.q:
Which is the better buy?
Pack A: 10 pencils for $2.50
Pack B: 24 pencils for $5.28
c: Both cost the same per pencil
items.e: Compare the price for 1 pencil, not the total price. Pack A: $2.50 ÷ 10 = $0.25 per pencil. Pack B: $5.28 ÷ 24 = $0.22 per pencil. Pack B costs less per pencil, so it is the better buy. (Pack A costs less in total, but you get less.)

items.q:
Which is the better buy?
Carton A: 12 eggs for $3.60
Carton B: 18 eggs for $5.40
c: Both cost the same per egg
items.e: Compare the price for 1 egg, not the total price. Carton A: $3.60 ÷ 12 = $0.30 per egg. Carton B: $5.40 ÷ 18 = $0.30 per egg. The unit prices are equal, so neither is a better buy.

items.q:
Which is the better buy?
Pack A: 4 cups of yogurt for $2.00
Pack B: 6 cups of yogurt for $3.30
c: Both cost the same per cup
items.e: Compare the price for 1 cup, not the total price. Pack A: $2.00 ÷ 4 = $0.50 per cup. Pack B: $3.30 ÷ 6 = $0.55 per cup. Pack A costs less per cup, so it is the better buy.

items.q:
Which bag of rice costs the least per pound?
2-pound bag: $3.00
5-pound bag: $6.50
10-pound bag: $12.00
c: They all cost the same per pound
items.e: Find each price per pound: 2-pound bag: $3.00 ÷ 2 = $1.50 per pound; 5-pound bag: $6.50 ÷ 5 = $1.30 per pound; 10-pound bag: $12.00 ÷ 10 = $1.20 per pound. The lowest unit price is $1.20 per pound, so the 10-pound bag is the best buy.

items.q:
Which bag of apples costs the least per pound?
3-pound bag: $4.35
5-pound bag: $6.95
8-pound bag: $11.60
c: They all cost the same per pound
items.e: Find each price per pound: 3-pound bag: $4.35 ÷ 3 = $1.45 per pound; 5-pound bag: $6.95 ÷ 5 = $1.39 per pound; 8-pound bag: $11.60 ÷ 8 = $1.45 per pound. The lowest unit price is $1.39 per pound, so the 5-pound bag is the best buy.

items.q:
Which pack of water costs the least per bottle?
6-pack: $3.00
12-pack: $5.40
24-pack: $11.04
c: They all cost the same per bottle
items.e: Find each price per bottle: 6-pack: $3.00 ÷ 6 = $0.50 per bottle; 12-pack: $5.40 ÷ 12 = $0.45 per bottle; 24-pack: $11.04 ÷ 24 = $0.46 per bottle. The lowest unit price is $0.45 per bottle, so the 12-pack is the best buy.

items.q: Leo walks 6 miles in 2 hours. Emma walks 10 miles in 4 hours. Who walks faster?
c: Both walk at the same rate
Cannot tell, the times are different
items.e: Find each unit rate. Leo: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 miles per hour. Emma: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5 miles per hour. Leo has the greater unit rate. (Emma walks farther in total, but takes more time.)

items.q: Car A goes 165 miles in 3 hours. Car B goes 240 miles in 4 hours. Which car is faster?
c: Both drive at the same rate
Cannot tell, the times are different
items.e: Find each unit rate. Car A: 165 ÷ 3 = 55 miles per hour. Car B: 240 ÷ 4 = 60 miles per hour. Car B has the greater unit rate.

items.q: Eli types 150 words in 3 minutes. Jack types 245 words in 5 minutes. Who types faster?
c: Both type at the same rate
Cannot tell, the times are different
items.e: Find each unit rate. Eli: 150 ÷ 3 = 50 words per minute. Jack: 245 ÷ 5 = 49 words per minute. Eli has the greater unit rate. (Jack types more words in total, but takes more time.)

items.q: Owen runs 3 miles in 30 minutes. Sam runs 5 miles in 50 minutes. Who runs faster?
c: Both run at the same rate
Cannot tell, the times are different
items.e: Find each unit rate. Owen: 3 ÷ 30 = 0.1 mile per minute. Sam: 5 ÷ 50 = 0.1 mile per minute. The unit rates are equal, so they run at the same rate.

items.q: Faucet A fills 12 gallons in 4 minutes. Faucet B fills 25 gallons in 10 minutes. Which faucet fills faster?
c: Cannot tell, the times are different
Both fill at the same rate
items.e: Find each unit rate. Faucet A: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 gallons per minute. Faucet B: 25 ÷ 10 = 2.5 gallons per minute. Faucet A has the greater unit rate. (Faucet B fills more water in total, but takes more time.)

items.q: Recipe A uses 2 cups of sugar for 3 cups of flour. Recipe B uses 3 cups of sugar for 4 cups of flour. Which recipe uses more sugar for each cup of flour?
items.e: Sugar per cup of flour: A: 2 ÷ 3 = 23 cup. B: 3 ÷ 4 = 34 cup. 23 = 812 and 34 = 912, so Recipe B uses more sugar per cup of flour.

items.q: Car A drives 336 miles on 12 gallons of gas. Car B drives 300 miles on 10 gallons. Which car goes farther on 1 gallon?
items.e: Miles per gallon: A: 336 ÷ 12 = 28. B: 300 ÷ 10 = 30. Car B goes farther on each gallon. (Car A goes more miles in total, but it uses more gas.)

items.q: Luis earns $45 for 4 hours of work. Lily earns $56 for 5 hours. Who earns more per hour?
c: They earn the same per hour
items.e: Luis: $45 ÷ 4 = $11.25 per hour. Lily: $56 ÷ 5 = $11.20 per hour. Luis earns $0.05 more per hour, even though Lily earns more in total.

items.q: An 18-ounce jar of peanut butter costs $3.60. A 12-ounce jar costs $2.76. How much less per ounce does the better buy cost?
items.e: 18-ounce jar: $3.60 ÷ 18 = $0.20 per ounce. 12-ounce jar: $2.76 ÷ 12 = $0.23 per ounce. $0.23 − $0.20 = $0.03 less per ounce. ($0.84 is the difference of the total prices.)

items.q: Store A sells 4 pounds of bananas for $2.36. Store B sells 3 pounds for $1.86. What is the lower price per pound?
items.e: Store A: $2.36 ÷ 4 = $0.59 per pound. Store B: $1.86 ÷ 3 = $0.62 per pound. The lower price per pound is $0.59, at Store A.

items.q: A 2-pound bag of rice costs $3.00 and a 5-pound bag costs $6.50. Zoe says the 2-pound bag is the better buy because $3.00 is less than $6.50. What should she compare?
items.e: Compare the price per pound. 2-pound bag: $3.00 ÷ 2 = $1.50 per pound. 5-pound bag: $6.50 ÷ 5 = $1.30 per pound. The 5-pound bag is the better buy.

sets.title: Word problems: use a unit rate (distance, time and cost)

items.q: A car travels at 60 miles per hour. How far does it go in 4 hours?
items.e: Distance = speed × time: 60 × 4 = 240 miles. (15 divides instead of multiplying; 64 adds.)

items.q: Mia walks 6 miles in 2 hours. At the same rate, how far can she walk in 5 hours?
items.e: Unit rate first: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 miles per hour. Then 3 × 5 = 15 miles. (30 multiplies 6 × 5 without finding the rate; 9 just adds 3 more.)

items.q: 6 muffins cost $9.00. At the same price, how much do 10 muffins cost?
items.e: Unit price: $9.00 ÷ 6 = $1.50 per muffin. 10 × $1.50 = $15.00. ($13.00 adds $4 for 4 more muffins; $90.00 multiplies $9.00 × 10.)

items.q: A printer prints 30 pages per minute. How long does it take to print 210 pages?
items.e: Time = pages ÷ pages per minute: 210 ÷ 30 = 7 minutes. Check: 30 × 7 = 210.

items.q: It took 7 hours to mow 4 lawns. At that rate, how many lawns can be mowed in 35 hours?
items.e: 35 hours is 35 ÷ 7 = 5 times as long, so mow 5 × 4 = 20 lawns. (The rate is 47 lawn per hour, and 47 × 35 = 20.) 5 lawns forgets to multiply by 4.

items.q: A car gets 32 miles per gallon. How many gallons does it need to drive 224 miles?
items.e: Gallons = miles ÷ miles per gallon: 224 ÷ 32 = 7 gallons. Check: 7 × 32 = 224.

items.q: Oranges cost $1.25 per pound. How many pounds can Maya buy with $10.00?
items.e: Pounds = money ÷ price per pound: 10.00 ÷ 1.25 = 1,000 ÷ 125 = 8 pounds. Check: 8 × $1.25 = $10.00. (12.5 multiplies 10 × 1.25.)

items.q: Sofia earns $36 for 3 hours of dog walking. At the same rate, how much does she earn for 8 hours?
items.e: Unit rate: $36 ÷ 3 = $12 per hour. 8 × $12 = $96.00. ($41.00 adds 5 for 5 more hours; $288.00 multiplies $36 × 8.)

items.q: A tank holds 120 gallons of water. It drains at 8 gallons per minute. How long does it take to empty?
items.e: Time = gallons ÷ gallons per minute: 120 ÷ 8 = 15 minutes. Check: 8 × 15 = 120.

items.q: 3 pens cost $2.25. At the same price, how much do 12 pens cost?
items.e: Unit price: $2.25 ÷ 3 = $0.75 per pen. 12 × $0.75 = $9.00. Or: 12 pens is 4 times 3 pens, so 4 × $2.25 = $9.00. ($11.25 adds $9 for 9 more pens.)

items.q: A train goes 65 miles per hour for 3 hours, then 55 miles per hour for 2 hours. How far does it go in all?
items.e: Find each part: 65 × 3 = 195 miles and 55 × 2 = 110 miles. 195 + 110 = 305 miles. (300 uses the average of the speeds, 60 × 5, but the train spent more time at 65 mph.)

items.q: Ava reads 120 pages in 4 hours. Nora reads 175 pages in 7 hours. How many more pages per hour does Ava read?
items.e: Ava: 120 ÷ 4 = 30 pages per hour. Nora: 175 ÷ 7 = 25 pages per hour. 30 − 25 = 5 more pages per hour. (55 is the difference of the totals.)

items.q: Ben walks at 3 miles per hour. How long will it take him to walk 7.5 miles?
items.e: Time = distance ÷ speed: 7.5 ÷ 3 = 2.5 hours. Check: 3 × 2.5 = 7.5 miles. (22.5 multiplies; 0.4 is 3 ÷ 7.5, the wrong way.)

items.q: Water flows from a hose at 4 gallons per minute. How many gallons flow out in 1 hour?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 4 × 60 = 240 gallons. (15 is 60 ÷ 4; 4 gallons is only 1 minute.)

items.q: A 12-pack of water costs $4.80. At the same price per bottle, how much do 30 bottles cost?
items.e: Unit price: $4.80 ÷ 12 = $0.40 per bottle. 30 × $0.40 = $12.00. ($0.40 is the price of only 1 bottle; $22.80 adds $18 for 18 more bottles.)

items.q: A plane flies 1,800 miles in 4 hours. At that rate, how far does it fly in 6 hours?
items.e: Unit rate: 1,800 ÷ 4 = 450 miles per hour. 450 × 6 = 2,700 miles. (450 is the distance in only 1 hour.)

items.q: A recipe uses 34 cup of sugar for each batch. How much sugar is needed for 6 batches?
items.e: Multiply the unit rate by the number of batches: 6 × 34 = 184 = 4 12 cups. (6 34 adds; 8 is 6 ÷ 34.)

items.q: Omar uses 2 cups of flour to make 12 pancakes. How much flour does he need for 30 pancakes?
items.e: Flour per pancake: 2 ÷ 12 = 16 cup. 30 × 16 = 5 cups. Or: 30 is 2 12 times 12, so 2 × 2 12 = 5. (20 adds 18 for 18 more pancakes; 6 is 12 ÷ 2, pancakes per cup.)

items.q: Noah runs 1 mile in 8 minutes. At that rate, how many miles can he run in 40 minutes?
items.e: Every 8 minutes is 1 mile. 40 ÷ 8 = 5 miles. (320 multiplies 40 × 8.)

items.q: Store A sells 5 pounds of oranges for $6.00. Store B sells 3 pounds for $3.90. Ruby needs 15 pounds. How much does she save by buying them at the store with the lower unit price?
items.e: Store A: $6.00 ÷ 5 = $1.20 per pound. Store B: $3.90 ÷ 3 = $1.30 per pound. 15 pounds: 15 × $1.20 = $18.00 at A and 15 × $1.30 = $19.50 at B. $19.50 − $18.00 = $1.50. ($0.10 is the saving on only 1 pound.)
